question: Who was the only person who remained president of the Indian National Congress for 6 years continuously before Independence of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was an Indian scholar and senior leader of the Indian National Congress during the Indian independence movement.
 
• He served as the President of the Indian National Congress for an extended period, specifically from **1940 to 1946**.
 
• Azad was one of the prominent leaders who advocated for **Hindu-Muslim unity** and played a crucial role in the freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• He was a close confidant of Mahatma Gandhi and a firm believer in the principles of **non-violence and civil disobedience**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• The Indian National Congress is one of the two major political parties in India, founded in 1885. It was the principal leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• The INC played a pivotal role in the freedom struggle, advocating for civil rights and self-rule, and later became the ruling party of independent India.
 
• Key leaders of the INC included figures such as Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
 
 
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad's Contributions**
 
 
• Azad was a scholar, writer, and a prominent advocate for education. He was instrumental in the establishment of the Indian Institutes of Technology and the foundation of the University Grants Commission (UGC).
 
• He served as India's first Minister of Education from 1947 to 1958 and was responsible for shaping the educational landscape of modern India.
 
• Azad was a proponent of the idea that education should be accessible to all, and he worked tirelessly to improve literacy rates and educational standards in the country.
 
 
 
• **INC Presidents Pre-Independence**
 
 
• Several prominent leaders served as the President of the INC before India's independence, including Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Motilal Nehru.
 
• Each of these leaders contributed significantly to the freedom struggle and the shaping of India's political and social landscape.
 
 
 
• **Hindu-Muslim Unity**
 
 
• One of the core principles advocated by Maulana Azad was the unity between Hindus and Muslims, which he believed was essential for the success of the independence movement.
 
• Despite the communal tensions, Azad consistently promoted the idea of a united India where people of different religions could coexist peacefully.
